title: Power Platform: Dataverse audit events sent to Purview no longer carry before-and-after values
summary: The removal of field values, retained Dataverse access and differing Microsoft dates are supported. The auditing control needs correction: its API only reads settings, and the documented UI now requires Global Audit Settings before Start Auditing.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Risk assessment
claims.claim: Dataverse audit events sent to Purview no longer include before-and-after field change values.
claims.quote: Starting in May 2026, Dataverse will no longer include before-and-after field change values in the audit events that are sent to Microsoft Purview.

claims.claim: Create and update events, including before-and-after column values, remain captured in Dataverse audit logs.
claims.quote: In Dataverse audit logs, create and update events—including a column’s before-and-after values—are captured. These values remain in Dataverse audit logs, but aren’t sent to Purview activity logging.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes preventing leaks of sensitive customer data, including financial, medical and personal information.
claims.quote: Examples of sensitive customer data include financial information, medical and health data, and personally identifiable information.

claims.claim: Audit events continue flowing to Purview after field-level values are removed.
claims.quote: Audit events will continue to flow to Purview; however, the detailed field-level value changes will be excluded.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Purview continues receiving metadata identifying who made changes.
claims.quote: Purview continues receiving audit event metadata (such as who made changes, the date of the changes, and the tables affected), but field-level value changes will no longer be included.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Purview continues receiving the dates of changes.
claims.quote: Purview continues receiving audit event metadata (such as who made changes, the date of the changes, and the tables affected), but field-level value changes will no longer be included.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Purview continues receiving metadata identifying the affected tables.
claims.quote: Purview continues receiving audit event metadata (such as who made changes, the date of the changes, and the tables affected), but field-level value changes will no longer be included.

claims.claim: Dataverse continues storing and exposing before-and-after changes through native audit APIs and tables.
claims.quote: Dataverse continues to store and expose before-and-after field changes through its native audit APIs and tables.

claims.claim: The Learn notice dates the start to May 2026 rather than the roadmap's June target.
claims.quote: Starting in May 2026, Dataverse will no longer include before-and-after field change values in the audit events that are sent to Microsoft Purview.

claims.claim: The roadmap uses the broader wording that all customer data is removed before audit events are sent to Purview.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters
claims.claim: The removal is on without an administrator enabling it.
claims.quote: Starting in May 2026, Dataverse will no longer include before-and-after field change values in the audit events that are sent to Microsoft Purview.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Microsoft asks administrators to update downstream workflows to retrieve detailed audit information directly from Dataverse.
claims.quote: Update your monitoring or downstream workflows to retrieve detailed field-level audit information directly from Dataverse, not from Purview.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Purview monitoring that depends on comparing old and new values stops working, including anomaly-detection rules.
claims.quote:
those solutions will stop working once this deprecation takes effect. Examples include:

- Rules that compare old/new values for anomaly detection.

claims.claim: Microsoft names pipelines analysing field-level deltas as affected solutions.
claims.quote: - Data pipelines that analyze field-level deltas.

claims.claim: Microsoft names custom compliance checks running in Purview as affected solutions.
claims.quote: - Custom compliance checks running in Purview.

claims.claim: The notice requires no changes for solutions that already use Dataverse audit logs as their source of truth.
claims.quote: No changes are required if your solution uses Dataverse audit logs as the source of truth.

claims.claim: Microsoft says removal reduces exposure of sensitive business or personal information through downstream systems.
claims.quote: Removing detailed field-level values from Purview-bound audit events reduces the risk of exposing sensitive business or personal information through downstream monitoring or analytics systems.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Manage Dataverse auditing says that columns with auditing turned off send before-and-after values as an asterisk.
claims.quote: When you turn off auditing for a column, the before-and-after values are sent as an "\*" to Microsoft Purview.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: The activity logs page says column-level secured fields are sent to Purview with an asterisk.
claims.quote: Column-level secured fields are sent to Purview activity logging with an asterisk (\*).

claims.claim: Users need the View Audit Summary privilege to use the Audit Summary view.
claims.quote: Users need the View Audit Summary privilege to see the Audit Summary view.

claims.claim: The audit detail retrieval messages require prvReadRecordAuditHistory.
claims.quote: To use these messages, ensure you have the prvReadRecordAuditHistory and prvReadAuditSummary privileges.

claims.claim: The audit detail retrieval messages require prvReadAuditSummary.
claims.quote: To use these messages, ensure you have the prvReadRecordAuditHistory and prvReadAuditSummary privileges.

claims.claim: Viewing Power Platform activity logs in Purview requires Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs rather than the Dataverse privileges used for native audit details.
claims.quote: To view Power Platform activity logs in Microsoft Purview, users need to be assigned either the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs role.

claims.claim: The path for controlling whether environment auditing is on ends at Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Audit and logs > Audit settings.
claims.quote: Select Global Audit Settings to open the Microsoft Dynamics 365 system settings. From there, turn on Start Auditing and select the entities you want to audit.
claims.fix: Narrow row 1's governs text to 'Whether Dataverse auditing is on for an environment'. Replace its UI path with 'Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Audit and logs > Audit settings > Global Audit Settings > Start Auditing', keeping the existing docs URL. Apply this to front matter and the rendered table. In Governance guidance, remove 'and Read logs' from the instruction that refers to row 1, since the corrected row covers environment auditing.

claims.claim: The organizations GET query is the automation counterpart for turning environment auditing and Read logs on or off.
claims.quote:
Retrieve organization settings

Use the following queries to retrieve your organization settings.

Change organization settings

Change the column values in the organization table to change how auditing works for the environment.
claims.fix: For the row narrowed to environment auditing in the UI finding, replace the call with 'PATCH [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/organizations([Organization ID])'. Replace 'The call reads the organization settings' with 'The request body sets isauditenabled to enable or disable environment auditing.' Keep https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/developer/data-platform/auditing/configure as docs, and update the rendered table too. Do not describe this operation as setting Read logs.

claims.claim: The printed GET query reads the organization auditing settings.
claims.quote:
GET [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/organizations?$select=
auditsettings,
isauditenabled,
auditretentionperiodv2,
isuseraccessauditenabled,
useraccessauditinginterval HTTP/1.1

claims.claim: A model-driven app exposes Audit Summary through Settings > Advanced Settings > System > Auditing > Audit Summary view.
claims.quote: From the app, select the Settings icon on the banner, select Advanced Settings, and then select System > Auditing > Audit Summary view.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: GET /api/data/v9.2/audits(<audit id>)/Microsoft.Dynamics.CRM.RetrieveAuditDetails retrieves audit details including field changes.
claims.quote:
Use this message to retrieve the audit details for a single audit record.

GET [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/audits(12869c65-d7d3-ec11-b656-281878f0eba9)/Microsoft.Dynamics.CRM.RetrieveAuditDetails

claims.claim: Changing audit settings requires the System Administrator or System Customizer role, or equivalent permissions.
claims.quote: You must have a system administrator or system customizer role or equivalent permissions to turn auditing on or off.

claims.claim: Dataverse user access or activity logging is sent to Purview for production environments only.
claims.quote: User access or activity logging is sent to Purview for production environments only.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a licensing entitlement specific to the removal of field values.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Dataverse before after field values Purview removal change license price meter' and 'Microsoft Purview Dataverse activity logging licensing Office 365 E1 E3 E5 audit requirements'; read the removal notice, activity logs overview and Purview service description. No removal-specific licence.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost; Open questions
claims.claim: Neither the roadmap nor the notice publishes a separate meter or price for this removal.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Dataverse before after field values Purview removal change license price meter'; read the roadmap, removal notice, Power Platform activity logs overview and Microsoft Purview service description. No meter or price for removing these values was stated.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The option to turn on audit logging is visible only when minimum Office licensing requirements are met.
claims.quote: The option to turn on audit logging is only visible when the minimum Office licensing requirements are met.

claims.claim: Dataverse stores audit logs and they consume log storage capacity.
claims.quote: Dataverse stores audit logs and they consume log storage capacity.

claims.claim: Dataverse audit information is available through Audit History, Audit Summary and the Web API.
claims.quote: You can view audit logs in the Audit History tab for a single record and in the Audit Summary view for all audited operations in a single environment. You can also retrieve audit logs by using the web API or the SDK for Microsoft .NET.

claims.where: Governance controls: Enable SAS Logging in Purview path
claims.claim: Enable SAS Logging in Purview is under Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Privacy and Security > Storage Shared Access Signature (SAS) Security Settings.
claims.quote:
Expand the Product list and select Privacy and Security.
7. In the Storage Shared Access Signature (SAS) Security Settings section, toggle the Enable SAS Logging in Purview setting to On.

claims.where: Governance controls: Enable SAS Logging in Purview explanation
claims.claim: Enable SAS Logging in Purview gives Purview access to each selected production environment's activity logs.
claims.quote: A Power Platform system admin or customizer needs to configure auditing in the Power Platform admin center and then turn on the Enable SAS Logging in Purview setting for each Power Platform production environment so Microsoft Purview auditing solutions can access the environment's activity logs.

claims.claim: The documented audit controls do not restore field values to Purview, and the notice gives no restoration step.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Dataverse removal before after field values Purview May 2026 opt out enable disable restore licensing meter'; read the removal notice, Configure auditing, Manage Dataverse auditing and activity logs overview. No restoration control found; retrieval reads native Dataverse audit data.

claims.claim: The Learn notice describes no opt-in or opt-out for removing field values.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Dataverse removal before after field values Purview May 2026 opt out enable disable restore licensing meter'; read the complete removal notice and the auditing configuration and activity logging pages. No removal-specific opt-in or opt-out found.

claims.claim: The published Purview customer engagement schema still describes Fields as containing created or updated values.
claims.quote: | Fields | Edm.String | No | JSON of Key Value pair reflecting the values that were created or updated |

claims.claim: The removal notice describes no new action on records or users.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Dataverse removal before after field values Purview May 2026 opt out enable disable restore licensing meter'; read the complete removal notice, which describes excluding field values and updating downstream workflows, not changing records or acting on users.
